bill_text.text_with_changes:
A bill for an act relating to agriculture; establishing the biofuel sales volume incentive program; authorizing rulemaking; appropriating money; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 41A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[+[41A.115] BIOFUEL SALES VOLUME INCENTIVE PROGRAM. +]

[+Subdivision 1.+]

[+Establishment.+]

[+Beginning January 1, 2028, the commissioner of agriculture must establish and administer a biofuel sales volume incentive program to provide financial incentives to retail gasoline stations for sales of eligible biofuel blends occurring during the previous calendar year. +]

[+Subd. 2.+]

[+Definitions.+]

[+For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given: +]

[+(1) "commissioner" means the commissioner of agriculture; +]

[+(2) "eligible biofuel blend" means a blend of gasoline and ethanol that contains 11 to 15 percent denatured ethanol by volume; and +]

[+(3) "retail gasoline station" means a retail business location that sells gasoline to end users from fuel dispensers for use in motor vehicles. +]

[+Subd. 3.+]

[+Incentive payments.+]

[+The commissioner must provide incentive payments of five cents per gallon of eligible biofuel blend sold at a retail gasoline station eligible under subdivision 4, not to exceed $50,000 per year. +]

[+Subd. 4.+]

[+Eligibility.+]

[+A retail gasoline station is eligible for incentive payments if the retail gasoline station: +]

[+(1) is located in Minnesota; +]

[+(2) is not a fleet operator; +]

[+(3) is operating and dispensing eligible biofuel blend at the retail gasoline station at the time of application; +]

[+(4) has not sold eligible biofuel blend before January 1, 2028; +]

[+(5) submits monthly reports as required under section 239.791, subdivision 8; and +]

[+(6) has not received money under the AGRI Biofuels Infrastructure Grant Program. +]

[+Subd. 5.+]

[+Application.+]

[+A retail gasoline station must apply for incentive payments in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner and must include: +]

[+(1) the volume in gallons of eligible biofuel blend sold during the calendar year; +]

[+(2) copies of fuel sales records; and +]

[+(3) any additional information required by the commissioner. +]

[+Subd. 6.+]

[+Verification.+]

[+The commissioner must verify reported sales volumes against fuel sales reports submitted to the Department of Commerce pursuant to section 239.791, subdivision 8. +]

[+Subd. 7.+]

[+Payments.+]

[+The commissioner must make payments on a first-come, first-served basis within the limits of available funding. +]

[+Subd. 8.+]

[+Rulemaking.+]

[+The commissioner may adopt rules to implement this section. +]

Sec. 2. [+APPROPRIATION; BIOFUEL SALES VOLUME INCENTIVE PROGRAM. +]

[+$5,000,000 in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of agriculture to administer the biofuel sales volume incentive program in Minnesota Statutes, section 41A.115. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2032. +]
bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to agriculture; establishing the biofuel sales volume incentive program; authorizing rulemaking; appropriating money; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 41A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[41A.115] BIOFUEL SALES VOLUME INCENTIVE PROGRAM.

Subdivision 1.

Establishment.

Beginning January 1, 2028, the commissioner of agriculture must establish and administer a biofuel sales volume incentive program to provide financial incentives to retail gasoline stations for sales of eligible biofuel blends occurring during the previous calendar year.

Subd. 2.

Definitions.

For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given:

(1) "commissioner" means the commissioner of agriculture;

(2) "eligible biofuel blend" means a blend of gasoline and ethanol that contains 11 to 15 percent denatured ethanol by volume; and

(3) "retail gasoline station" means a retail business location that sells gasoline to end users from fuel dispensers for use in motor vehicles.

Subd. 3.

Incentive payments.

The commissioner must provide incentive payments of five cents per gallon of eligible biofuel blend sold at a retail gasoline station eligible under subdivision 4, not to exceed $50,000 per year.

Subd. 4.

Eligibility.

A retail gasoline station is eligible for incentive payments if the retail gasoline station:

(1) is located in Minnesota;

(2) is not a fleet operator;

(3) is operating and dispensing eligible biofuel blend at the retail gasoline station at the time of application;

(4) has not sold eligible biofuel blend before January 1, 2028;

(5) submits monthly reports as required under section 239.791, subdivision 8; and

(6) has not received money under the AGRI Biofuels Infrastructure Grant Program.

Subd. 5.

Application.

A retail gasoline station must apply for incentive payments in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner and must include:

(1) the volume in gallons of eligible biofuel blend sold during the calendar year;

(2) copies of fuel sales records; and

(3) any additional information required by the commissioner.

Subd. 6.

Verification.

The commissioner must verify reported sales volumes against fuel sales reports submitted to the Department of Commerce pursuant to section 239.791, subdivision 8.

Subd. 7.

Payments.

The commissioner must make payments on a first-come, first-served basis within the limits of available funding.

Subd. 8.

Rulemaking.

The commissioner may adopt rules to implement this section.

Sec. 2. APPROPRIATION; BIOFUEL SALES VOLUME INCENTIVE PROGRAM.

$5,000,000 in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of agriculture to administer the biofuel sales volume incentive program in Minnesota Statutes, section 41A.115. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2032.
additions: Beginning January 1, 2028, the commissioner of agriculture must establish and administer a biofuel sales volume incentive program to provide financial incentives to retail gasoline stations for sales of eligible biofuel blends occurring during the previous calendar year.
For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given:
(2) "eligible biofuel blend" means a blend of gasoline and ethanol that contains 11 to 15 percent denatured ethanol by volume; and
(3) "retail gasoline station" means a retail business location that sells gasoline to end users from fuel dispensers for use in motor vehicles.
The commissioner must provide incentive payments of five cents per gallon of eligible biofuel blend sold at a retail gasoline station eligible under subdivision 4, not to exceed $50,000 per year.
A retail gasoline station is eligible for incentive payments if the retail gasoline station:
(3) is operating and dispensing eligible biofuel blend at the retail gasoline station at the time of application;
(4) has not sold eligible biofuel blend before January 1, 2028;
(5) submits monthly reports as required under section 239.791, subdivision 8; and
(6) has not received money under the AGRI Biofuels Infrastructure Grant Program.
A retail gasoline station must apply for incentive payments in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner and must include:
(1) the volume in gallons of eligible biofuel blend sold during the calendar year;
(2) copies of fuel sales records; and
(3) any additional information required by the commissioner.
The commissioner must verify reported sales volumes against fuel sales reports submitted to the Department of Commerce pursuant to section 239.791, subdivision 8.
The commissioner must make payments on a first-come, first-served basis within the limits of available funding.
The commissioner may adopt rules to implement this section.
APPROPRIATION; BIOFUEL SALES VOLUME INCENTIVE PROGRAM.

$5,000,000 in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of agriculture to administer the biofuel sales volume incentive program in Minnesota Statutes, section 41A.115. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2032.
